name: Eteocretan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: undeciphered fragmentary inscriptions; no stress description possible

sources.note: Five certain inscriptions (Dreros, Praisos; late 7th/early 6th to 3rd c. BC), two bilingual; language untranslated. Only phonological remark: 'Komn and lmo seem to show that /n/ and /l/ could be syllabic.' No mention of stress or accent.

sources.citation: Natalia Elvira Astoreca. 2021. Early Greek Alphabetic Writing: A Linguistic Approach. Oxford: Oxbow (CREWS vol. 5), open access.
sources.note: Comparative graphematics; Eteocretan alphabet cited for letter shapes/values (e.g. the sign for /dz/ or /ts/, citing Duhoux 1982: 165 f.). Nothing on Eteocretan stress.

sources.citation: Henri Van Effenterre. 1989. De l'étéocrétois à la selle d'agneau. BCH 113(2).
sources.note: First page only. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: J. Faucounau. 1985. Les inscriptions étéocrétoises à la lumière du schéma kretschmérien. L'Antiquité Classique 54.
sources.note: First page only; speculative affiliation. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Maurice Leroy. 1984. Review of Y. Duhoux, L'étéocrétois. Les textes. La langue. L'Antiquité Classique 53: 455-457.
sources.note: Only p. 455 text is exposed in the Persée HTML (PDF blocked by altcha). Says Duhoux offers only 'transcriptions phonétiques de type large' (κ, γ may be palatal/velar/uvular; ζ = /ts/ or /dz/) and distinguishes archaic (7th-6th c.) and late (4th-2nd c.) periods. Nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Raymond A. Brown. 2003-. Eteocretan language pages (web; based on his 1982 Birmingham M.Litt thesis, printed as Brown 1985, Evidence for pre-Greek speech on Crete from Greek alphabetic sources, Amsterdam: Hakkert). Wayback snapshot 2025-11-14 of carolandray.plus.com/Eteocretan/
sources.note: No statement on stress. Dreros #1 page: sonorants 'occur in positions which suggest they may be syllabic or that there may be a svarabhakti vowel, e.g. κομν... and possibly λμο'. Praisos #1: 'possibly... another example of syllabic sonorant ρ (r) between two kappas'. Only 'accent' mention concerns the Greek accentuation of the place-name Praisos (Πραῖσος vs Πραισός uncertain).

sources.citation: Yves Duhoux. 1981. Les Étéocrétois et l'origine de l'alphabet grec. L'Antiquité Classique 50: 287-294.
sources.note: First page only; alphabet origin. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Michel Lejeune. 1947. L'inscription Isaluria de Drèros: étéocrétois ou crétois? Revue des Études Anciennes 49: 274-285.
sources.note: First page only (Persée HTML); on whether the Dreros text is Eteocretan or Greek. Nothing on stress.
Extinct, unclassifiable; refs = Duhoux 1982 and Romashko 2020 (both hhtype 'minimal'). Nothing on stress.
